svg.title: A family f(t) has comparison price C at radius p if every such measure satisfies ∥P j cjf(tj)∥≤rC. This is the precise signed-combination bound used here. If f(t) = P n(t/p)nan with P n ∥an∥≤C, the bound follows by interchanging a finite sum and an absolutely convergent series. Conversely, define the moment vector ((t/p)n)n in l∞. The signed-combination bound defines a bounded linear map on their span and then its closure. Coordinate vectors belong to that closure: subtract the already recovered lower coordinates from the moment vector at a small nonzero t, divide by (t/p)n, and let t →0. Its image supplies the coefficients. Restricting from radius p to p′ < p sums the geometric coefficient majorant and gives an absolutely convergent series. This is the recovery step used to turn signed-combination bounds into analytic line estimates.
